text:
MPC rose modestly today as oil prices stabilized after last week's sharp decline. U.S. crude fell nearly 8% the prior week on hopes of U.S.-Iran talks, but those negotiations collapsed when Trump rejected Iran's ceasefire proposal on September 26th. With renewed tension in the Middle East now expected, oil prices have steadied—U.S. crude is holding at $96.41 per barrel—which supports refiner margins. Refineries are running at 94% capacity, a healthy operating level for a refiner like MPC.

The stock's modest bounce follows a steeper two-week slide of 0.6%, reflecting the whipsaw from geopolitical uncertainty. Saudi Arabia is ramping crude exports despite ongoing attacks on its infrastructure, which has helped stabilize global supply, but the risk of further U.S.-Iran escalation remains a source of volatility for energy investors.
